title: Compatibility contract, staged deprecation lifecycle, and migration tooling for serving runtime
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Objective: Define a clear, implementable compatibility contract for the serving runtime that prescribes what changes require a major version, the deprecation timeline for field/API removals, and the rollout gating and migration tooling required to safely evolve the runtime across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Scope covers: public REST/gRPC control-plane APIs, runtime binary compatibility surface (protocols, artifacts), model serving wire contracts (prompt/response schema, headers), SDK contract guarantees, and rollout automation for canary/cascade upgrades.

Policy highlights (summary):
- Versioning model: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with additional channel labels (e.g., 2.1.0, 2.1.0-lts, 2.1.0-rc). Major increments reserved for breaking changes as defined below.
- Breaking change definition: Any user-observable change that can cause existing requests, integrations, or persisted recordings (e.g., cached KV artifacts, offline client libraries) to fail, produce semantically different outputs, or change billing/latency SLAs without a documented opt-in. Examples: removing an API endpoint, changing required header semantics, changing default tokenizer/encoding incompatibly, altering response JSON schema keys, or changing behavior of rollout/gating toggles.
- Deprecation window: Minimum 90 days public deprecation notice for any non-emergency removal on Hosted. Dedicated and Private customers receive 180 days notice and a compatibility shim where feasible. Deprecation notices must include migration steps, sample diffs, and automated compatibility checks.
- Opt-in experimental features: Feature flags must be behind opt-in booleans and be explicitly marked experimental; their removal is allowed with 14 days notice if no customers have opted in.
- API compatibility strategy: Maintain a compatibility matrix that maps supported server versions to client SDK versions and documented runtime capabilities. Backwards-compatibility guarantee: servers in the same MAJOR will accept requests issued by clients up to two MINOR versions older; forward compatibility is best-effort and must be documented.
- Rollout gates and automation: Every runtime release that includes behavior changes must pass a standardized set of gate checks (unit/integration compatibility suite, canary traffic probes, regression evals on seeded prompts, cost/latency baseline checks). Canary must run on 1% of traffic for 48 hours with automated rollback triggers on error rate, latency regressions, or quality drop beyond thresholds.
- Migration tooling: Provide a CLI and server-side agent that can: run client-to-server compatibility scans, flag deprecated API usage, run a dry-run migration mode with live traffic replay, and provide suggested code diffs and SDK patch notes.

Deliverables for this ticket:
1) The textual policy document and a short checklist for engineers (this ticket).
2) A machine-readable compatibility matrix schema (separate ENG ticket to implement).
3) A minimal migration-lint prototype in the repo that scans code for deprecated patterns (follow-up ticket).

Operational constraints: Private deployments can stage upgrades offline; policy includes an explicit section for air-gapped upgrade procedures and customer communication templates. Hosted API will publish deprecation headers (Deprecation: version=2.0, removal-date=2026-07-01) and a docs page with migration playbooks.

Rationale and tradeoffs: We choose a conservative deprecation window to reduce customer disruption and align with Dedicated/Private sales commitments. A more permissive removal policy would let us iterate faster but raises outage risk for enterprise customers. The compatibility matrix complexity is traded off against automation — the long-term aim is to generate matrix entries from CI compatibility tests to avoid manual authoring.
acceptance_criteria: A human-readable policy doc checked into docs/runtime/versioning/compatibility-policy.md and linked from the release checklist
Defined breaking-change examples and a published deprecation timeline template
Checklist of automated gate checks with owners and thresholds documented
Proof-of-concept migration lint tool added to repo under tools/migration-lint with README
Canary/rollback thresholds codified and a sample canary job in k8s/ci that runs the gate suite
